status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text

characters.name: The Angel of the Presence

verses.note: God commands the angel of the presence to write for Moses the whole history from creation to the building of the sanctuary - the book's own frame device.
The angel begins dictating the account of creation to Moses at God's word.
Names the four places sanctified on earth: Eden, the Mount of the East, Sinai, and Zion.

funFacts: Nearly the entire book of Jubilees is framed as this angel's direct speech to Moses on Sinai, making him the narrator of everything from Genesis through the Exodus.

characters.name: Adam

verses.note: Adam wakes and names Eve, taken from his rib.
Adam tills the Garden of Eden for seven years before the serpent tempts Eve.
Adam dies at the close of the nineteenth jubilee, the first man buried in the earth, seventy years short of one thousand.

ageEvents.age: 930 (per the text, seventy years short of 1000)

funFacts: The text explains Adam's death age by reading Genesis 2:17 ('in the day thou eatest thereof thou shalt die') against the rule that a thousand years is as one day.

verses.note: The serpent tempts Eve, who eats the fruit and gives it to Adam.

characters.name: Cain

verses.note: Cain slays Abel because God accepted Abel's sacrifice and not his own.
Cain marries his sister Awan and builds the first city, named for his son Enoch.
Cain is killed when his own house collapses on him, killed by a stone as he had killed Abel with a stone - 'righteous judgment' by the same instrument rule.

funFacts: Jubilees is explicit that Cain's death by a collapsing house is direct poetic-justice retribution, citing a 'heavenly tables' law that a killer dies by the same means he used.

verses.note: God accepts Abel's sacrifice, not Cain's, precipitating the murder.
Born after Adam and Eve mourn Abel four weeks of years; named because God 'raised up a second seed' in place of Abel.

characters.name: Enoch (son of Jared)

verses.note: First man to learn writing; records the order of months, weeks, jubilees, and sees the future in a vision.
Dwells with the angels six jubilees of years, learns the rule of the sun, and testifies against the Watchers who defiled themselves with human women.
Taken from among men into the Garden of Eden itself, where he continues writing the judgment and wickedness of mankind.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION: this Enoch (Jared's son, taken up alive) is a different person from Cain's son Enoch (4:9), after whom Cain's city is named - see notes.

verses.note: Born to Enoch and Edni in the twelfth jubilee.
Fathers Lamech, who will father Noah.

characters.name: Noah

verses.note: Born to Lamech, named for comfort from the cursed ground.
Prays to God after the Flood that evil spirits not be allowed to destroy his grandsons.
Writes down the medicines taught him by the angels and gives the book to his beloved son Shem.
Dies at 950 years, buried on Mount Lubar in Ararat - second in righteousness only to Enoch.

funFacts: Jubilees credits Noah with writing the first book of medicine, taught to him directly by angels to counter the demons Mastema was allowed to keep.

verses.note: Receives Noah's book of medicines as his eldest and best-loved son.

characters.name: Prince Mastema

verses.note: Asks God to leave him a tenth of the malignant spirits to carry out his will on the sons of men; God grants nine parts bound, one part left under Mastema.
Comes before God and accuses Abraham of loving Isaac too much, prompting the command to sacrifice him - Jubilees' own name for Genesis 22's unnamed tempter.
Attempts to slay Moses on his way back to Egypt, and later helps the Egyptian magicians oppose Moses before Pharaoh.

funFacts: 'Mastema' is Hebrew for 'hatred' or 'hostility' - Jubilees is one of the earliest texts to give a personal name and court role to the Genesis-adjacent figure later Christian tradition calls Satan.

characters.name: The Tower of Shinar
characters.purpose: Explains the origin of the confusion of tongues and the name 'Babel' - narrated as the Lord's own direct act witnessed by the angel of the presence, not delivered through any human character.

verses.note: Peleg names his son Reu because the children of men have taken up building a city and tower in Shinar; they build it, saying 'let us ascend thereby into heaven.'
They build for forty-three years with fire-baked brick and asphalt cement.
The Lord declares He will confound their language so they cannot understand one another, descends with the angel of the presence to see the city and tower, and confounds their speech.
The land of Shinar is named Babel for this confusion; the Lord sends a mighty wind that overthrows the tower, and the builders are dispersed from Shinar in the thirty-fourth jubilee.

funFacts: Jubilees gives the tower a precise, almost architectural account (forty-three years of building, exact brick/cubit measurements) that Genesis 11 never supplies.

characters.name: Abraham

verses.note: As a young man Abram separates himself from his father's idol-worship and begins to pray to the Creator alone.
Abram burns the house of idols by night, and his brother Haran dies trying to save them from the fire.
Mastema accuses Abraham's love for Isaac before God, and Abraham is found faithful in every trial including this one.
Blesses and instructs Jacob at length before his death.

funFacts: Jubilees adds that Abram's own brother Haran died attempting to rescue idols from the fire Abram set - Genesis never explains Haran's death, this text supplies a cause.

verses.note: Sees Ishmael playing and grows jealous, demanding Hagar and Ishmael be cast out so Isaac alone will inherit.
Sent away with Ishmael into the wilderness of Beersheba; an angel shows her a well when the water runs out.
Grows into an archer in the wilderness of Paran and takes an Egyptian wife, fathering Nebaioth.

characters.name: The Covenant Sign
characters.purpose: God's command that Abraham and every male of his household be circumcised on the eighth day as an eternal token of the covenant; Abraham personally carries it out the same day he receives it.

verses.note: The Lord tells Abraham to keep the covenant and circumcise every male among him, on the eighth day, as an eternal token; the uncircumcised soul will be cut off for breaking the covenant.
Abraham circumcises Ishmael, all born in his house, and all bought with his money; he himself is circumcised the same day.
The text states this law is for all generations forever, with no day of the eight ever omitted, engraved on the heavenly tables.

funFacts: This chapter is also where God renames Sarai to Sarah and first names the coming son Isaac, folded into the same covenant scene as the circumcision command.

verses.note: Weaned at a great banquet Abraham holds in his honor.
Carries the wood up the mountain with Abraham, not knowing he is the offering, until spared by the angel's voice.
In old age remains sorrowful and housebound while his sons fight the Amorite kings, too grieved to leave with them.

characters.name: Rebecca

verses.note: Warns Jacob against marrying a Canaanite woman as Esau has done.
Delivers an extended blessing over Jacob, a testament in her own voice absent from the Genesis account, praising him above Esau.

funFacts: Jubilees gives Rebecca her own full deathbed-style testament and blessing scene for Jacob, a speech Genesis never records her making.

characters.name: Jacob

verses.note: Dreams of the ladder at Bethel while fleeing Esau toward Laban's house.
Leads six thousand men to rescue his sons from seven Amorite kings who ambushed them near Shechem, killing all seven kings personally.
Journeys to Egypt in old age to be reunited with Joseph.

funFacts: Jubilees turns the brief Genesis mention of trouble with the Amorites into a full battle narrative where Jacob personally kills seven named kings.

verses.note: Bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulon, and Dinah to Jacob.
Dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath, and is buried there.
Reuben lies with her while Jacob is away, an act the text treats at length as a grave sin.
Dies of mourning the same month she hears Joseph has perished, and is buried beside Rachel's tomb.

characters.name: Levi

verses.note: With Simeon, executes judgment on the men of Shechem for the defilement of Dinah.
Because of his zeal at Shechem, the seed of Levi is chosen for the priesthood and recorded on the heavenly tables as blessed forever.
Jacob dresses Levi in priestly garments at Bethel and consecrates him, and Levi receives the tithe.

funFacts: Jubilees frames the Shechem massacre - which Jacob himself curses in Genesis 49:5-7 - as the very act that earns Levi the priesthood; a striking moral divergence from Genesis worth flagging, not smoothing over.

verses.note: Joins Levi in slaying the men of Shechem.

characters.name: Dinah (daughter of Jacob)

verses.note: Carried off and defiled by Shechem, son of Hamor, at age twelve - the act that triggers the chapter's law against intermarriage.
Dies the same month as Joseph and Bilhah, and is buried beside Rachel's tomb.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION: not the same Dinah as Mahalalel's wife in 4:15, an antediluvian ancestor six generations before the Flood - see book notes.

verses.note: Lies with Bilhah, his father's concubine, while Jacob is away at Beersheba; Jacob learns of it and never again lies with Bilhah.
The text expands this into a full legal ruling condemning a man who uncovers his father's bed, prescribing death for both parties under the law.

characters.name: Joseph

verses.note: Sent by Jacob to check on his brothers at Shechem; they sell him to Ishmaelite merchants who bring him to Potiphar in Egypt.
His brothers dip his coat in a kid's blood and send it to Jacob, who mourns believing an evil beast devoured him.
His father's grief on the tenth of the seventh month becomes the text's own explanation for the origin of the Day of Atonement fast.
Rules Egypt eighty years, dies at 110, and makes Israel swear to carry his bones out of Egypt at the exodus.

funFacts: Jubilees explicitly ties the origin of the Day of Atonement fast to Jacob's grief over Joseph's supposed death - an etiology Leviticus never gives.

verses.note: Takes Tamar, a daughter of Aram, as a wife for his firstborn Er.
Mistakes the veiled Tamar for a harlot at Timnah and leaves his ring, necklace, and staff as a pledge for payment.
Orders Tamar burned for apparent whoredom, then recognizes his own pledge tokens and confesses 'Tamar is more righteous than I am.'
Veils herself and sits by the road to Timnah after Judah's wife withholds Shelah from marrying her.
Sends Judah's own ring, necklace, and staff to prove whose child she carries rather than be burned.

characters.name: Moses

verses.note: Born during Pharaoh's decree to cast Hebrew male infants into the river; hidden three months, then set adrift in a pitched ark.
Found by Tharmuth, Pharaoh's daughter, who has Jochebed nursed as his wet-nurse before raising him at court.
Slays an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, then flees after a fellow Israelite throws the killing back in his face.

funFacts: Because the whole book is framed as speech directed at Moses, his own birth story is narrated in second person - 'thou wast born,' 'thy mother hid thee.'

verses.note: Hides Moses three months, then sets him adrift in an ark and nurses him secretly by night.
Hired by Tharmuth, unknowingly, to nurse her own son.
Guards the ark by day, watching for birds.
Offers to fetch a Hebrew nurse for the infant, and brings her own mother Jochebed.

characters.name: Tharmuth

verses.note: Pharaoh's daughter, finds the infant Moses in the river and has compassion on him.

funFacts: Jubilees is the source of the name 'Tharmuth' for Pharaoh's daughter - the name is not given in Exodus itself.

characters.name: The Passover Ordinance
characters.purpose: The Lord's direct second-person command to Moses to remember and observe the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month forever, retelling the night the plague passed over Israel in Egypt and fixing the ordinance's exact timing and manner.

verses.note: Moses is told to remember the commandment concerning the Passover, celebrated the fourteenth of the first month, the night Mastema's powers slew Egypt's firstborn.
The blood on the lintels is the sign that spares a house; all Israel eats the paschal lamb and is ready to leave Egyptian bondage.
Moses is commanded to observe the day every year without fail, as an eternal ordinance engraved on the heavenly tables.
Fixes the exact permitted window for slaying and eating the lamb, between the evenings, with any leftover flesh burned before morning.

funFacts: Jubilees credits Mastema's loosed powers, not simply 'the LORD,' with executing the plague on Egypt's firstborn - the same court-appointed adversary introduced back in chapter 10.

characters.name: The Reckoning of Weeks and Jubilees
characters.purpose: The book's own calendrical polemic: a fixed 364-day solar year of exactly 52 weeks, engraved on the heavenly tables and tied to Noah's feast of weeks, defended against the lunar reckoning the text says will cause Israel to 'go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and feasts.'

verses.note: The feast of weeks, celebrated in heaven since creation, was kept by Noah and his sons, then Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, until Israel forgot it and renewed it at Sinai.
The angel states the reckoning is written in 'the book of the first law' and lays out the four new-moon memorial days and the year's division into thirteen-week quarters, fifty-two weeks total.
Moses is commanded to instruct Israel to observe a 364-day year exactly, since neglecting it will dislodge every feast and sabbath from its proper season.
Warns that a lunar-based reckoning (arriving ten days too soon each year) will lead Israel to confound holy and unclean days, and to keep feasts 'after the error' of the Gentiles.

funFacts: This calendrical argument - a fixed 364-day/52-week solar year against lunar timing - is Jubilees' own stated reason for existing, and it recurs throughout the book far beyond this one chapter.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list to avoid inventing detail the text doesn't give.

antediluvianGenerations.note: Full Adam-to-Noah genealogy with named wives for every generation (Awan, Azura, Nedam, Mfialéléth, Dinah daughter of Baraki'el [antediluvian, distinct from Jacob's daughter Dinah], Baraka, Edni, Edné, Béténds/Betends) - listed individually for genealogy tracing but most given no independent acts beyond begetting, so not promoted to full character entries.

enochSonOfCain.note: Cain's son, namesake of the first city Cain builds. A different person from the patriarch Enoch (Jared's son) given a full entry above - flagged as a naming collision, not merged.

noahsSonsBeyondShem.note: Ham and Japheth and their many named sons (Cush, Mizraim, Canaan, Madai, etc.) divide the earth by lot after Babel; Canaan's disobedience in settling Lebanon instead of his allotted portion is the text's own explanation for why Canaan is under a standing curse. Kept as a bulk reference since the text's interest is the land division itself, not individual biography.

sevenAmoriteKings.note: Seven kings of the Amorites (names given in corrupted form in the source text, e.g. '+Arésa+', 'Taphti', 'Sarégn') ambush Jacob's sons at Shechem and are slain by Jacob; kept as a collective military-antagonist reference rather than individual entries since the names are not reliably legible from the extracted text.

jacobsDaughtersInLawCh34.note: A full list of named wives taken by Jacob's remaining sons after Joseph's presumed death (Reuben's Adi, Simeon's Adiba'a, Levi's Melka, Judah's Bétast'él, and others) - logged in bulk since the text gives them names but no further acts.

All four verse sets were read directly from the source file (not invented) and use its real, if occasionally OCR-garbled, chapter/verse structure. Everything else (all person-tier characters, the original book-level notes on Jubilees' distinctive content, naming collisions, and OCR corruption caveats) is unchanged from the prior draft and remains accurate on re-check. Every scribeTiers[].managerId now resolves to a real characters[].id, every parentManagerId resolves or is null, and every law character's deliveredBy resolves to a real character or is explicitly null with a stated reason.
